Evelyn — thanks for the questionnaire and the deadline flag. Neha, Jonas and Karthik are copied for specifics; I own the final review and delivery.

Summary answers below (we'll also attach the completed PDF and a short policy excerpt):

1) Data residency: Hosted API request logs and transient payloads are stored in the cloud region that serves the request by default (AWS us-west-2, us-east-1; GCP us-central1 available on request). We maintain region metadata with every record and can provide region-scoped copies on dedicated accounts.

2) Retention windows:
- Request metadata and audit logs: default 365 days; configurable by account (30–730 days).
- Generated text responses: default 30 days in application cache; 90 days in audit blob store for troubleshooting (encrypted at rest).
- Embeddings: retained 180 days by default if customer opts into embedding storage; otherwise ephemeral and not persisted beyond request pipeline.

3) Erasure process & SLA:
- Customer-initiated erasure request triggers three steps: mark-for-deletion in active stores (within 4 hours), purge from primary databases (within 24–72 hours depending on shard/region), and scheduled scrub of backups during next backup retention window (up to 30 days).
- SLA for full surface erasure (active + primary + index removal): 30 calendar days; backlog cases escalated to Neha on the security operations team. We provide a signed attestation when deletion completes.

4) Geo-fencing / region lock:
- We support account-level region-locking for hosted customers; requests are routed and stored only in allowed regions. Geo-lock must be requested during onboarding and enforced via routing policy and VPC endpoints.

Attachments: we'll attach our retention policy extract and the completed questionnaire PDF. If you want narrower retention windows or a different erasure SLA (e.g., expedited 7-day purge), we can include that in a contractual addendum.

Adding a couple of implementation notes for clarity:

- Backups: encrypted daily snapshots retained for a maximum of 30 days by default; backups are geo-redundant across two regions for high-availability accounts. Backup retention is separate from primary retention windows and is included in the 30-day backup purge SLA mentioned above.

- Embeddings: technical detail — embeddings that are stored are indexed in a separate vector-store; we delete index entries and underlying vectors as part of the erasure workflow and rotate encryption keys every 90 days.

- Evidence for SOC2 / audit: we can provide redacted log extracts and deletion attestations; full raw logs require an executed NDA and appropriate controls.
